reason: Re-opened packet.js veda 8 --verse 1.62.3 (and 1.62.2 for context): the evidence stands verbatim in the ākhyāna that opens Sāyaṇa’s comment (atredam ākhyānam): Saramā the devaśunī, the cows carried off by the Paṇis, Indra sends her to track them as a hunter looses a dog, she will go only if her child gets the milk-food of those cows (tadgosaṃbandhi kṣīrādyannam), he agrees; he then glosses dhāsim as annam for her own son. Every part of the reading is in his words, in his sequence; Wilson note b agrees. Plain sense checked against day.js: 1.62.2 has Indra ‘through whom our sires, Angirases … found the cattle’, and 1.62.3 continues the finding; ‘tells of the search’ is not Griffith’s word (he has ‘desired it’) but 1.62.2’s ‘knowing well the places’ carries the tracking, so it does not land. No four words of the key. verse.js ok (Rig Veda 1.62.3, at [61,3]); entry-check ok. Yāska has only the name (Nirukta 11.24), not this verse. No school, comparison or tone issue.
